Class BaseModPlugin

java.lang.Object
com.fs.starfarer.api.BaseModPlugin
All Implemented Interfaces:
ModPlugin
Direct Known Subclasses:
CoreLifecyclePluginImpl
public class BaseModPlugin extends Object implements ModPlugin
Extend this class instead of implementing ModPlugin for convenience if you do not intend to implement all the methods. This will also help avoid your mod breaking when new methods are added to ModPlugin, since default implemenations will be added here and your implementation will inherit them.

While having a ModPlugin for your mod is not strictly necessary, it serves as an entry point for all kinds of useful things, such as faction initialization, adding custom scripts and picking AI plugins.

You need to instruct the game to load your implementation of this class by e.g. adding it to your mod_info.json: "modPlugin":"my.package.name.MyModBasePlugin"

    • afterGameSave

      public void afterGameSave()
      Called after a game is saved.
      Code in here gets executed after the game gets saved. The main use for this is in combination with beforeGameSave. If you did clean-up code in beforeGameSave, you can re-add your stuff in here.

      Example:

          
        Global.getSector().getListenerManager().addListener(new MyListener());
      Specified by:
      afterGameSave in interface ModPlugin

    • beforeGameSave

      public void beforeGameSave()
      Called before a game is saved.
      Code in here gets executed before the game gets saved. This is mainly useful for doing cleanup. Anything that is part of the sector gets serialized when the game is saved. If you, for instance, add custom listeners to the sector and the game gets saved, they are added to the save file. If you then later e.g. rename the class of those listeners, that will break mod compatibility and users won't be able to upgrade your mod in an ongoing campaign. Also, players won't be able to remove your mod from an ongoing campaign. To avoid this issue, you can simply clean up anything that you added to the sector that doesn't need to be saved in this method and then re-add it in the afterGameSave-method.

      Example:

          
                while (Global.getSector().getListenerManager().hasListenerOfClass(MyListener.class)){
            Global.getSector().getListenerManager().removeListenerOfClass(MyListener.class);
        }
      Specified by:
      beforeGameSave in interface ModPlugin

    • onGameLoad

      public void onGameLoad(boolean newGame)
      Called after a game has been loaded. Also called when a new game is created, after the onNewGame() plugins for all the mods have been called.

      In here, you should do all kinds of initialization logic, such as adding transient scripts, registering campaign plugins, adding custom sensor ghosts etc.

      Specified by:
      onGameLoad in interface ModPlugin
      Parameters:
      newGame - if true, a new campaign has just been started. Sector generation logic should only be executed if this is true.

    • onNewGameAfterEconomyLoad

      public void onNewGameAfterEconomyLoad()
      Called after the economy is loaded from economy.json and the initial steps are taken. At this point, calling get getMarket() on entities will return the proper market. The sequence of calls is: onNewGame(); // can add markets to the economy here programmatically //load economy and step it onNewGameAfterEconomyLoad();

    • pickShipAI

      public PluginPick<ShipAIPlugin> pickShipAI(FleetMemberAPI member, ShipAPI ship)
      Called to pick an AI implementation for a specific ship. Here instead of in CampaignPlugin to support custom AI for missions.

      Example:

          
                if(ship.getVariant().getHullVariantId().equals("myVariantId")){
            return new PluginPick(new MyAi(), CampaignPlugin.PickPriority.MOD_GENERAL)
        }
        return null;

      Specified by:
      pickShipAI in interface ModPlugin
      Parameters:
      member - fleetMemeber of the ship in question. Can be used to inform your decision if/which AI to choose
      ship - the ship in question
      Returns:
      a plugin pick containing the chosen ship AI, or simply null to use the default AI

    • pickWeaponAutofireAI

      public PluginPick<AutofireAIPlugin> pickWeaponAutofireAI(WeaponAPI weapon)
      Called to pick an AI implementation for a specific weapon.
      This code gets executed whenever the game selects an autofire AI for a weapon, which is usually at start of combat This is mainly relevant if your weapon has some quirks that the regular AI doesn't understand.

      Example:

          
        if(weapon.getId().equals("myWeaponId")){
            return new PluginPickinvalid input: '<'>(new MyAi(), CampaignPlugin.PickPriority.MOD_GENERAL);
        }
        return null;

      Specified by:
      pickWeaponAutofireAI in interface ModPlugin
      Parameters:
      weapon - the weapon in question
      Returns:
      a plugin pick containing the chosen AI, or simply null to use the default

    • pickMissileAI

      public PluginPick<MissileAIPlugin> pickMissileAI(MissileAPI missile, ShipAPI launchingShip)
      Called to pick missile AI implementation.
      This method is how you can assign custom AI to missiles. If you want to write your own missile AI, I would recommend having a look at the MagicMissileAI available in MagicLib for inspiration.

      Example:

          
        if(missile.getProjectileSpecId().equals("myMissileProjId")){
            return new PluginPickinvalid input: '<'>(new MyAi(), CampaignPlugin.PickPriority.MOD_GENERAL);
        }
        return null;
      Specified by:
      pickMissileAI in interface ModPlugin
      Parameters:
      missile - the missile in question. This is usually the main deciding factor.
      launchingShip - the ship that launched the missile. This can usually be ignored
      Returns:
      a plugin pick containing the chosen AI, or simply null to use the default
